provenance: Related by family in the project brief that founded this archive. To be re-captured in Larry's own words. 2026-09-13, his son's account of where the designation came from: the early conversations with Larry, before anything was typed as he spoke. He may have misunderstood. He remembers Larry mentioning Bien Hoa in that conversation, and thinks Larry may have mentioned a "118th AOD" there, which he took to be Larry's own unit. He found some of the stories hard to follow.
text: He remembers his organization as the 118th AOD — Aviation Operations Detachment. He describes the organization as relatively small, approximately 110 men, including radio operators and pathfinders. Some personnel reportedly required special clearances.
researchNotes: The designation "118th AOD" is remembered terminology and may not be exactly correct. Candidate organizations to research include the 118th Aviation Company and Aviation Operations Detachments generally. 2026-09-13: THE ATTRIBUTION IS WEAK. By his son's own account (see provenance), "118th AOD" is his reading of an early, untyped, hard-to-follow conversation that also mentioned Bien Hoa, and it may not have been offered as Larry's own unit. That matters because the 118th Aviation Company, the leading candidate the brief's number pointed to, was based at Bien Hoa. A story about Bien Hoa that named the 118th would produce exactly this record without Larry ever calling it his unit. Against it, in Larry's transcribed words: "18th Aviation" three times (2026-08-23, 2026-09-12, 2026-09-13; his son certain each time it was 18th), the third time as the host of the van, with his own unit "so small, I don't think we even had a medic". Nothing is withdrawn: the brief stays as given, and "118th AOD" also stands in the founding larrysRecollection on his person record, which is not edited (rule 1). But no one should weigh "118th" as Larry's firm memory against his own "18th". The approximately 110 men, radio operators and pathfinders, and special clearances come from the same brief and carry the same caveat. If Larry now names his own unit's number cold, that will be the first capture of it in his words. Ledger #2; research/units/18th-aod-stars-and-stripes-1964.md.
